transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

It could be the battery, but intermittent cutting out after just a few seconds often points to the vacuum’s protection system kicking in. This usually happens if the airflow is still restricted (even slightly damp filters or a hidden blockage) or if the battery voltage drops suddenly under load. Since you’ve already cleaned the filter and checked for obvious blockages, I need to know how it behaves when charging and exactly what lights are showing when it stops.

It charges fine and the charger light comes on, shows full blue lights when done. When it cuts out the blue lights sometimes flash a few times, sometimes nothing at all. No red lights. It's usually fine straight off the charger but worse once the battery's been partly used.

Dyson vacuums in 'Boost' or 'Max' mode drain the battery very quickly—often just a few minutes—which is normal behaviour, not a fault. If it was on Boost, switching to Normal mode should fix the short run time. However, if it cuts out after 5-10 seconds even on Normal mode with a full charge, that points more strongly to the battery struggling to deliver voltage under load or a subtle airflow restriction tripping protection. Please try running it on Normal mode right after a full charge and let me know how long it lasts.

On Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. In handheld mode with no tool it still cuts out sometimes, just less often. I haven't tried a timed run on normal mode yet - is it worth me doing that before deciding on a battery?

It is absolutely worth doing that test first. Running on Max (Boost) mode will drain any battery in just a few minutes—that is normal behaviour and not a fault. If the vacuum cuts out after only 5–10 seconds even on Normal mode, it suggests the battery can no longer sustain the voltage required under load, which is very common for a 5-year-old Dyson. Please run it on Normal mode from a full charge and tell me exactly how long it lasts.

I haven't done a timed run on Normal yet, so I can't give you a figure. The battery isn't hot or swollen, if that matters. If it still cuts out within seconds on Normal from a full charge, is that enough to say it's the battery and worth the £60+?

Yes—if it cuts out within seconds on Normal mode from a full charge, that is effectively enough to confirm the battery has failed and needs replacing. There is little point in further checks; proceed with the battery replacement.

candidates: Thermal cut-out from residual blockage or damp filter (medium)
